outline.unique_angle: A first-person RN anecdote with a concrete, reproducible failure (grapefruit + a named drug, three specific interactions MIMS caught that the AI missed) plus a portable decision rule — 'interaction questions never touch general AI.' Top-3 are either broad listicles or general-public health-advice explainers; none show a real clinician's cross-check workflow or compare a general LLM directly against a specialist pharma database from a bedside-practice viewpoint.

warnings: YMYL health topic — must follow CLAUDE.md rule 5: RN byline + reg #, 1+ PubMed/.gov citation (BJCP DDI study PMID 39359001 is a strong fit), 'last reviewed' date, no medical-advice phrasing ('in my practice' / 'ask your supervisor'). fact-checker must run before publish.
AI Overview likely steals top-of-page real estate for the broad query — only competitive if the post wins on depth + a concrete anecdote the Overview can't synthesize.
Do NOT make 'can ChatGPT check drug interactions' the primary keyword: its SERP is wall-to-wall DR 80-90 academic journals. Demote to a secondary/section target.

All DR and KD numbers here are ESTIMATES — no Ahrefs/Ubersuggest tool query succeeded this session (Ahrefs free tool returned no metrics, only instructional content). Volumes are inferred buckets, not tool-reported. Re-run with a logged-in tool before betting budget on this.
Cite MIMS carefully — MIMS is subscription/regional (AU/NZ/UK). For global readers also reference drugs.com / Stockley's so the rule generalises.
